translationLoss.rule: What counts toward the sap-loss tally
translationLoss.documentQuote: Sap-loss tally: the running total of all sap that leaves the stem, whether transpired or respired away.
translationLoss.explanation: This is a slight blur, not a lost rule. The definition names only two routes, transpired and respired, but the root-collar exit in step 4 is neither. Step 4 still states that rule outright: "If segment 1 is SINK-ACTIVE, its amount leaves the stem at the root collar. Add it to the sap-loss tally." The leaf-drop removal is also labeled "transpired away", which is a domain stretch, but the instruction to add it to the tally is explicit.

None were lost or added. Every abstract rule is present with the same threshold and order. Intake is uncapped. Spill-over runs in order 1 to 6, using "more than its holding volume", with a cascade, and segment 6's excess goes to loss. The mode check uses "at least" and "at most" with hysteresis and at most one change. Release uses quarter and half amounts that are "Work[ed] out ... before you change any segment" and then applied together; there is no cap, and the overfill is never corrected in cycle 5. The reset fires on "more than 38 (strictly greater)". The data table and the intake rows match the abstract exactly.

domainPull: The pull was strongest at step 4. The state named \"SINK-ACTIVE\" makes a segment a donor that sends half its sap down the phloem toward the root, but in botany a sink receives sap. On top of that, \"Leaf-drop\" and \"transpired away\" give a botanical label to an arbitrary halving when the total exceeds 38. Nobody fell for either.
preReadNamedTheBreak: n/a: nobody went wrong. All three reports match the true answer on final levels, modes, all 13 changes, resets [1,4] and loss 76. C's notes did flag the likeliest trap anyway: "SINK-ACTIVE segments are donors, not receivers, contradicting the botanical meaning of sink".
preReadEffect: It made no measurable difference. A, with no framing, and B, with framing but no pre-read, got the identical exact answer. The trap C identified in the sink direction caught none of the three. The pre-read did not prevent C's one execution slip, a temporary misaddition in the balance check that C fixed itself.
summary: All three operators reproduced the true answer exactly: final [6,10,9,7,4,2], segments 1 to 5 SINK-ACTIVE and segment 6 QUIET, all 13 changes, leaf-drops in cycles 1 and 4, and loss 76. Each also handled the cycle 5 boundary correctly, where the total is exactly 38 and no drop fires. Coherence carried through the plant vascular translation. The document kept every rule; the only blur is a definition of the sap-loss tally that leaves out the root-collar route, which step 4 states anyway. The only flaws are presentation slips in the balance check: A printed row 1 as 17 instead of 20, and C misadded and then corrected it.
